region.text: the Dali (Erhai) basin and the Six Zhao of Piluoge

ledger.note: 738: the Tang make Piluoge Prince of Yunnan, the year after he united the Six Zhao. 'In the year 737 AD, Piluoge united the Six Zhaos in succession'; the Tang granted him the name Meng Guiyi and the title 'Prince of Yunnan' in 738; infobox 'Established: 738'. The capital is Taihe from 739.

region.text: Nanzhao, Piluoge's united Six Zhao around Dali, under the Tang title

ledger.note: 738: Nanzhao enters the Tang order. 'In 738, the Tang granted Piluoge the Chinese-style name Meng Guiyi' and the title 'Prince of Yunnan'. The page does not call 738 vassalage or tribute (its 'amicable tributary relationship' is said of the later Nanzhao Kingdom), so the status is the author's reading of the Tang title; the Tang side calls it a tributary (tang-dynasty /ledger/51). Written from Nanzhao's side (counterpart is the suzerain, region Nanzhao's own shape), the mirror of tang-dynasty /ledger/51. The shape is Cliopatria's first (741), as in the found event.

region.text: the 32 native counties of Yunnan

ledger.note: 750: Nanzhao attacks the Tang. Geluofeng 'raised an army to capture 32 native counties of Yunnan and killed Zhang Qiantuo'; the Tang sent Xianyu Zhongtong with 60,000 men (751) and Li Mi with 70,000 (754).

region.text: the 32 native counties of Yunnan

ledger.note: 750: Nanzhao takes 32 counties of Yunnan. 'In 750, Geluofeng raised an army to capture 32 native counties of Yunnan.' Region: Cliopatria's step from the 741 to the 750 shape.

region.text: Nanzhao as Geluofeng left the Tang

ledger.note: 751: Nanzhao breaks with the Tang. Tianbao War page: Geluofeng 'proclaimed himself Eastern Emperor (東帝) and became the sworn younger brother of Tibetan Emperor Mé Aktsom, no longer loyal to the Tang dynasty' (undated there); Nanzhao page: Geluofeng 'launched the Tianbao War against the Tang dynasty', the Tang 'attacked Nanzhao with an army of 80,000 soldiers in 751' and were beaten at Xiaguan. The Tianbao War page dates the fighting from 750 ('In 750, Geluofeng raised an army to capture 32 native counties of Yunnan'), so the break may be a year earlier; 751 is kept to pair with tang-dynasty /ledger/52 (the author would put it at 750, the contest_start above). Written from Nanzhao's side (counterpart is the suzerain, region Nanzhao's own shape), the mirror of tang-dynasty /ledger/52.

region.text: the 32 native counties of Yunnan

ledger.note: 754: Li Mi's army is wiped out and the Tang cannot attack again. 'Pursued by the Nanzhao-Tibetan coalition, Li Mi's army was wiped out ... The Tang then lacked the strength to attack Nanzhao again.'

region.text: Nanzhao, the client and ally of the Tibetan Empire

ledger.note: 754: Nanzhao takes the Tibetan side. 'By the end of 754, Geluofeng had established an alliance with the Tibetans against the Tang that would last until 794'; 'Geluofeng accepted a Tibetan title and acted as part of the Tibetan Empire' (Nanzhao page). Tianbao War page: Li Mi's retreating army in 754 'was pursued by Nanzhao-Tibetan coalition forces, and his entire army was wiped out'. The year is the page's; reading the alliance as a client tint is the author's. The Tibetan Empire page has Nanzhao under Tibetan control from 750 (recorded in the tibetan-empire dossier), which is not followed here. Written from Nanzhao's side (counterpart is the suzerain, region Nanzhao's own shape), the mirror of tibetan-empire /ledger/25; the region is the 755 shape because that dossier uses it.

region.text: Yunnan east of the Erhai and the marches Cliopatria adds in 755

ledger.note: 755: the rest of Yunnan. Page silent: no opened page dates the step from 215,000 to 591,000 km2 (Yunnan east of the Erhai, Kunming, and the marches in Guizhou, Guangxi and the Vietnamese border); Cliopatria's 755 shape is the only evidence.

region.text: Yuesui Commandery (Xichang)

ledger.note: 756: Yuesui falls. 'Nanzhao captured Yuesui Commandery and the official Zheng Hui, who later became prime minister.' Region: the Xichang area, which Cliopatria adds only in 830.
779: the capital passes from Taihe to Yangjumie, both in the Dali basin (infobox 'Taihe (before 779) and Yangjumie (after 779)'); the same year Yimouxun joined a large Tibetan attack on the Tang.

region.text: Nanzhao, the client and ally of the Tibetan Empire

ledger.note: 794: Nanzhao breaks with Tibet. 'In 794, he launched the battle of Shenchuan to break up with Tibet and switched sides to the Tang.' (Nanzhao page; the Tianbao War page also dates the break from Tibet to 794 at Shenchuan.) Written from Nanzhao's side (counterpart is the suzerain, region Nanzhao's own shape), the mirror of tibetan-empire /ledger/42.

region.text: Nanzhao, which 'switched sides to the Tang' after Shenchuan

ledger.note: 794: Nanzhao returns to the Tang. 'In 794, he launched the battle of Shenchuan to break up with Tibet and switched sides to the Tang'; the Nanzhao page adds that the kingdom 'would later enter an amicable tributary relationship with the Tang' (undated). The year is the page's, the tributary status the author's reading; the attacks of 829-877 on this dossier's ledger show how loose it was. Written from Nanzhao's side (counterpart is the suzerain, region Nanzhao's own shape), the mirror of tang-dynasty /ledger/71.

region.text: the Chengdu plain

ledger.note: 829: Wang Cuodian attacks Chengdu. 'In 829, Wang Cuodian attacked Chengdu, but withdrew the following year.' Cliopatria draws the Chengdu plain as Nanzhao's from 830.

region.text: the Chengdu plain

ledger.note: 830: Nanzhao withdraws from Chengdu.

region.text: Annan (Songping, the Tang protectorate around Hanoi)

ledger.note: 863: Nanzhao takes Annan. In January it 'besieged Songping with about 50,000 men' and the city fell shortly after; the Nanzhao page: 'occupied Annan for three years'. Nanzhao-backed locals had held Songping briefly in 860-861.

region.text: Annan (Songping)

ledger.note: 866: Gao Pian retakes Annan. 'Gao completed the retaking of Annan in fall 866, executing the enemy general, Duan Qiuqian.'

region.text: Yuesui, Guizhou, Guangxi and the Vietnamese marches, the lands beyond Yunnan

ledger.note: 866: Nanzhao falls back to Yunnan. With Annan retaken the lands beyond Yunnan go from Cliopatria's shape; the Annan page has no extent for Guizhou or Guangxi; it says only 'Prior to Li Hu's arrival, Nanzhao had already seized Bozhou' (860) and, for 861, 'Li Hu retook Songping on 21 July but Nanzhao's forces moved around and seized Yongzhou'. [Author fix ea-04-b, 2026-10-19: the earlier wording 'at various points' is not on the page; the two sentences are quoted instead, re-read 2026-10-19.]

region.text: Qiongzhou, within 70 km of Chengdu

ledger.note: 873: Nanzhao invades Sichuan again. It 'reached within 70 km of Chengdu, and seized Qiongzhou' in 873-874; Gao Pian beat the remainder at the Dadu River in 875.

region.text: Qiongzhou and the Chengdu approaches

ledger.note: 875: Nanzhao is driven out of Sichuan. 'Gao Pian defeated the remaining Nanzhao troops at the Dadu River.'

region.text: Nanzhao, Piluoge's Six Zhao realm, in its last shape

ledger.note: 902: the tributary relation ends with the dynasty. 'In 902, the dynasty came to a bloody end when the chief minister (buxie), Zheng Maisi, murdered the royal family and usurped the throne' (Nanzhao page, infobox 'overthrown: 902'). The Tang itself fell in 907 (tang-dynasty ends the tint at 902 with /ledger/85); the page gives no separate end for the tribute, so the year is the dissolve's. Written from Nanzhao's side (counterpart is the suzerain, region Nanzhao's own shape), the mirror of tang-dynasty /ledger/85.

region.text: the Nanzhao land of 900, Dachanghe's from 902

ledger.note: 902: Zheng Maisi ends the Nanzhao. 'The chief minister (buxie), Zheng Maisi, murdered the royal family and usurped the throne' and renamed the state Dachanghe (infobox 'overthrown: 902').

wars.name: Tianbao War
wars.outcome: Nanzhao took 32 native counties in 750, was beaten step by step in 751-753, turned to Tibet, and with the Tibetans destroyed Li Mi's 70,000 in 754 (the Nanzhao page says Xianyu Zhongtong lost 80,000 at Xiaguan in 751 and Li Mi 100,000 in 754).
wars.note: Tibet's heavy taxes and military service led to the 794 Battle of Shenchuan.

wars.name: Nanzhao raids on the Pyu
wars.outcome: Raids intensified c. 800-802 and 808-809; Halin was overrun and its 3,000 people taken in 832; 'by 763 ... the upper Irrawaddy Valley' was conquered, but the page does not say Nanzhao held Pyu land afterwards, so no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Nanzhao attack on Chengdu
wars.outcome: Wang Cuodian attacked Chengdu in 829 and withdrew in 830.

wars.name: Tang-Nanzhao conflicts in Annan
wars.outcome: Raids from 846 and 858; Songping taken briefly in 860-861; besieged with 50,000 men in January 863 and held three years; Gao Pian won in September 865 and retook Annan in autumn 866.

wars.name: Nanzhao invasions of Sichuan
wars.outcome: Shilong besieged Chengdu in 869 for over a month; in 873-874 Nanzhao reached within 70 km of Chengdu and seized Qiongzhou; Gao Pian defeated it at the Dadu River in 875 and drove it out of Bozhou in 877.

wars.name: Battle of Shenchuan
wars.outcome: Yimouxun broke with Tibet and switched to the Tang; in 795 he attacked a Tibetan stronghold and in 801 the Battle of Dulu killed over 10,000 Tibetan-aligned soldiers.

certainty.note: No page gives Nanzhao's frontier as a line; the Tibetan, Tang and Pyu frontiers are approximate throughout, and the lands beyond Yunnan are the least certain.

notes:
Written 2026-10-19 by the ea-04-b research agent from five opened pages (Nanzhao, Tianbao War, Tang-Nanzhao conflicts in Annan, Dali Kingdom, Pyu city-states), the full page budget; the Tibetan Empire and Tang-Tibet relations pages opened for tibetan-empire are not cited here. The Nanzhao page's infobox has no area figure, so no infobox comparison is possible.

Cliopatria row: 'Nanzhao' 741..910, 9 shapes. The dossier starts in 738 (infobox 'Established: 738'; the text has Piluoge uniting the Six Zhao in 737 and the Tang title in 738) and ends in 902 (Zheng Maisi's coup). The last Cliopatria years 902-910 are Great Changhe (Dachanghe), written as a small dossier of its own (slug dachanghe) that carries the Nanzhao land to 937 through its renames (Datianxing, Dayining); the Kingdom of Dali row starts only in 947.

What the pages support and what they do not. Supported: the core around Dali (737-739), the 32 native counties of Yunnan (750), Yuesui (756), the Chengdu raid (829-830), Annan (863-866), the Sichuan invasions (869, 873-875), the end (902). Not supported by any opened page: the 755-865 shapes' lands in Guizhou (381 cells), Guangxi (289) and the Vietnamese marches (247 cells, 76 of them inside a 150 km disc around Hanoi), which Cliopatria draws; the Annan page says only that Nanzhao had seized Bozhou before 860 and, in 861, Yongzhou ('Li Hu retook Songping on 21 July but Nanzhao's forces moved around and seized Yongzhou'); the phrase 'at various points' that an earlier draft of this note used is not on the page. They are kept (verdict ok, unverified) and lost in one 866 ledger event. The Chengdu plain (213 cells in Cliopatria's 830-859 shape) is removed from the 830, 850 and 860 shapes because the page says Wang Cuodian 'attacked Chengdu, but withdrew the following year'; Yuesui (Xichang) is kept from 756 as the page's 'captured Yuesui Commandery'.

Disagreements: founding 737 (text) or 738 (infobox); capital Taihe 739 (text) with 'Taihe (before 779) and Yangjumie (after 779)' in the infobox; the Dali Kingdom page dates the Great Changhe 903-927, Great Tianxing 927-928 and Great Yining 928/929-937 where the Nanzhao page has 902-928, 928-929 and 929-937; the Tibetan alliance starts in 754 on the Nanzhao page and in 750 on the Tibetan Empire page ('under Tibetan control from 750 to 794'); the vassal tints (Tang 738-751 and 794-902, Tibet 754-794) are recorded in the tang-dynasty and tibetan-empire dossiers and, since the review, here as well (see the revision paragraph below).

Not drawn: the Pyu. The Pyu city-states page says 'By 763, the Nanzhao king Ko-lo-feng had conquered the upper Irrawaddy Valley' and that in 832 Nanzhao warriors overran the Pyu country and took 3,000 prisoners from Halin, but it adds that it does not say whether Nanzhao held Pyu land afterwards; Cliopatria's shapes hold no Upper Burma cell. The raids appear as a war with no zone. Also not drawn: the 808 title 'Ruler of the Pyu', the 830s conquests of 'Kunlun and Nuwang' and the 835 Michen campaign (not placed on any page), the 859-877 Bozhou raids, the 860-861 brief fall of Songping to locals backed by Nanzhao, the 869 siege of Chengdu.

Counterparts without a dossier: Dachanghe (written here), the Six Zhao (not a state), the Pyu city-states (Sri Ksetra, Halin; suggested slug pyu-city-states, a state group for Southeast Asia). Family: no Yunnan family exists in colours.json; 'southeast-asia' is the nearest (hue band 25-120), the same as the Dali Kingdom would take.

Gazetteer: all names resolve (Tali for Dali in Yunnan, since 'Dali' alone is also a Shaanxi town; Xichang for Yuesui; Chengdu; Hanoi for Songping/Annan). Songping, Yongzhou, Bozhou, Yuesui, Halin are not places in the gazetteer.

Author revision after the review (ea-04-b, 2026-10-19; Nanzhao, Tianbao War and Tang-Nanzhao conflicts in Annan pages re-read the same day): (1) Six vassal events were added, the review's blocking finding: 738 vassal_start tang-dynasty (c2), 751 vassal_end tang-dynasty (c2), 754 vassal_start tibetan-empire (c2), 794 vassal_end tibetan-empire (c3), 794 vassal_start tang-dynasty (c2), 902 vassal_end tang-dynasty (c2). They mirror tang-dynasty /ledger/51, 52, 71, 85 and tibetan-empire /ledger/25, 42. The region is Nanzhao's own Cliopatria shape of the year (741, 750, 755, 755, 755, 900); for 754 and 794 the 755 shape is used, not the 750 shape alive in 754, because tibetan-empire /ledger/25 and /42 use it. Convention question for the orchestrator: the schema reads 'counterpart is the vassal itself' for vassal events, so in the suzerain's dossier (tang-dynasty, tibetan-empire) the counterpart is Nanzhao; here, as the reviewer asked, the counterpart is the suzerain and the region is Nanzhao itself. A renderer that tints the region of every vassal_start in a dossier as that dossier's vassal would tint Nanzhao as its own vassal; these six events should feed the state page and the status timeline, and the tint should be drawn from the suzerain-side events. (2) Disagreements, with the pages: the 738 status rests on the Tang title only (the Nanzhao page calls the later kingdom, not the 738 relation, tributary); the break with the Tang is 750 on the Tianbao War page's fighting ('In 750, Geluofeng raised an army to capture 32 native counties of Yunnan') and the Nanzhao page's 751 Xiaguan, so 751 is kept only to pair with the Tang ledger; the Tibetan Empire page has Nanzhao under Tibet from 750 where the Nanzhao page has the alliance 'by the end of 754'. (3) The /ledger/11 (866) note and the notes above now quote the two Annan sentences about Bozhou and Yongzhou instead of the phrase 'at various points'. (4) Kept as they are, routed to ea-04-a (tang-dynasty): Annan 863-866 is an occupation here and a loss (tang /ledger/79) and a gain (/ledger/80) there; the types should agree (occupation_start/occupation_end there); tang-dynasty has no mirror for the 750 gain and contest, the 755 and 756 gains, the 829-830 Chengdu contest or the 873-875 Sichuan occupation. No page has been found for the 755 step (376,000 km2) or for how much of Guizhou and Guangxi Nanzhao held, so those stay confidence 1 and unverified; the Pyu war still has no zone.
